metadata.title: Two Hundred Applications, Thirty-One Days
metadata.subtitle: Episode 2 — the introduction: effort is not progress, and the two-sided rule for AI

series.role: the felt problem — Mira's allocation failure, the RCT behind the thesis, and the use-more/trust-less rule; assumes Episode 1 for the repo tour

metadata.purpose: A faithful reel of the book's Introduction: the opening case (two hundred applications against a thirty-one-day clock), the diagnosis (an allocation problem, not a motivation problem), the controlled trial that grounds it, the execution/judgment division, the two-sided instruction (use AI more aggressively AND trust it less), why a model cannot audit itself, and the concrete first trace the chapter hands the reader.
metadata.note: Greeting rotation: Hola taken by Ep1, Namaste reserved by the parked deep episode, Annyeong by the git-claude-code reel — Merhaba is fresh. DOUBLE-CHECK: every [verify]-flagged figure in the source chapter (the ~56% AI-skill premium, the ~82%/~21% screening rates, the Eightfold/Kistler litigation specifics) is narrated as MECHANISM ONLY and never appears on screen as a number or a named party. The Anthropic RCT figures and the OPT clock DO appear — both trace to primary sources in the book's own reference list. Mira's numbers are framed on screen as the book's opening scenario, never as a measured statistic. Episode 1 owns the repo tour and the three mechanisms (contract / gates / skip rate) — this episode must not re-teach them.
